short_summary: A live-action Poison Ivy television series is reportedly in early development for HBO, with Penguin showrunner Lauren LeFranc in discussions to produce.

sources.name: Polygon
sources.title: HBO Poison Ivy Show Reportedly Coming From 'The Penguin' Producer

sources.name: IGN
sources.title: Poison Ivy Show in Early Development with Penguin Showrunner in Talks to Produce

paragraphs: Fans of DC Comics characters can anticipate a new television project focused on one of Batman's most distinctive adversaries. According to recent reports, a live-action Poison Ivy series is currently in the early stages of development, with Lauren LeFranc in talks to serve as a producer. LeFranc previously worked as a showrunner and executive producer on HBO's acclaimed series The Penguin. Although she helped bring that gritty Gotham-adjacent drama to life, the upcoming Poison Ivy program will reportedly remain entirely separate from Matt Reeves' cinematic Batman universe and the associated spinoff shows, which collectively form the Batman Epic Crime Saga.

Industry observers note that the continuity surrounding DC adaptations remains famously complex, and it has not yet been confirmed whether the plant-controlling ecoterrorist will inhabit the broader DC Universe overseen by James Gunn or exist within an independent narrative framework. The initiative is still in its infancy. Sources indicate that no writers have been officially attached to the project yet, and casting announcements remain far off. The development process also experienced prior delays due to a corporate merger involving Paramount and Warner Bros. If the production ultimately moves forward and secures a green light, it is slated to air on HBO, mirroring the distribution home of The Penguin.

Poison Ivy, also known as Dr. Pamela Isley, has enjoyed various notable interpretations outside of comic books over the decades. Cinematic audiences famously remember her portrayal by Uma Thurman in the oft-derided 1997 film Batman & Robin, while contemporary viewers have grown accustomed to her animated adventures and romance in the Harley Quinn television series, where she was voiced by Lake Bell. The character has notably not yet appeared in any of the newer live-action cinematic projects spearheaded by DC Studios, leaving an open canvas for whoever eventually takes on the demanding role.

Meanwhile, the broader DC landscape continues to shift across various platforms. Other villain-centric cinematic efforts, such as Clayface, are making their way to theaters, while upcoming live-action Batman appearances in cinema remain years away, pending the arrival of DC Studios' The Brave and the Bold movie. At the same time, Matt Reeves' The Batman Part 2 recently paused filming while the director stepped away due to a personal matter, with Steven Soderbergh now helping finish the sequel for a February 2028 release. Whether the upcoming HBO series will eventually introduce other familiar figures from Gotham City, or how it will define the complex nature of Dr. Isley herself, remains to be seen as the production takes its very first steps.

facts.fact: A Poison Ivy television series is reportedly in early development with Lauren LeFranc in talks to produce it.
The series would be broadcast on HBO if picked up, but it is not connected to Matt Reeves' Batman films or The Penguin.
The project currently has no writers attached and was previously paused due to a corporate merger between Paramount and Warner Bros.
